parts.text: Which one of the following best describes **economic growth**?
choices: The pattern of rises and falls in real GDP over time around the long-term trend rate of growth
The stage of the economic cycle when real GDP grows rapidly above the trend rate, with low unemployment
An increase in the output of goods and services in an economy over time, measured by the change in real GDP
GDP divided by the population showing the average output per person

rows.answer:
Correct option: **C** (An increase in the output of goods and services in an economy over time, measured by the change in real GDP)
A: incorrect, that is the meaning of economic cycle
B: incorrect, that is the meaning of boom
D: incorrect, that is the meaning of GDP per capita

Last year, Istrova experienced rapid economic growth of 5.5%, while inflation rose to 6.0%.

Explain why faster economic growth might be accompanied by rising prices.

rows.answer:
Award 1 mark for identifying a relevant point, 1 mark for developing it and 1 mark for applying it to the context.

Example:
- Rapid growth increases total demand (1) and if supply cannot keep up, firms raise prices (1), so demand-pull inflation rises, as shown by inflation of 6.0% when growth reached 5.5% (1)

intro:
The economy of Rendova grew by 5.2% last year, one of the fastest rates in the region. New factories and mines have opened, but there are concerns about air pollution and the gap between rich and poor.

Real GDP per person in Rendova is R\$6,000. Employment rose by 387,000 last year. However, the richest 10% of households now receive 36% of income, up from 32% ten years ago.

Air quality in the capital exceeds safe limits on 94 days a year. Hospital admissions for breathing problems have risen. Tax revenue has increased, and the government has used some of it to build 470 new schools.

Energy prices have risen by 45% in a year. Consumer spending fell by 1% in the last quarter, and business investment by 6%. Unemployment has risen to 5.4%.

Inflation is currently 6.5%, mainly because of energy and food costs. Some retailers have started offering discounts to attract customers, while others say their costs are still rising.

parts.text: Which one of the following best describes **unemployment**?

intro:
Unemployment in Istrova has stayed at 7.0% for a year, even though there are 435,000 job vacancies. Many unemployed people lack the skills employers need. The government is launching new training programmes and offering help with travel costs to areas with jobs.

Unemployment is highest in former mining and steel towns in the north, at up to 14%, while in the capital it is 2%. Most vacancies are in technology, healthcare and construction. Average house prices in the capital are 5 times those in the north.

The training programmes will cost I\$406 million over three years and aim to retrain 61,000 people. Some economists say lower taxes for firms that move to the north would also help.

figures.label: Extract A
figures.text:
A recession in Corvana has caused unemployment to rise from 4.0% to 8.5% in one year. Construction and retail have been hardest hit.

254,000 people have lost their jobs in the past year. The budget deficit is already 4% of GDP, and national debt is 72% of GDP. Interest rates are 2%.

The government is considering a C€13bn programme of spending on roads, schools and housing. Business confidence is at its lowest for 8 years.
figures.provenance: Original fictional extract written for this question bank.

parts.text: Which one of the following best describes **inflation**?
choices: Inflation caused by total demand rising faster than the economy's ability to supply
A sustained rise in the general price level over a period of time
The year chosen as the reference point for a price index given a value of 100
A sustained fall in the general price level over a period of time

rows.answer:
Correct option: **B** (A sustained rise in the general price level over a period of time)
A: incorrect, that is the meaning of demand-pull inflation
C: incorrect, that is the meaning of base year
D: incorrect, that is the meaning of deflation

parts.text: Which one of the following best describes **deflation**?
choices: Inflation caused by rising costs of production such as wages or raw materials, passed on as higher prices
A sustained fall in the general price level over a period of time
The costs to firms of changing prices such as reprinting price lists and updating websites
Inflation caused by total demand rising faster than the economy's ability to supply

rows.answer:
Correct option: **B** (A sustained fall in the general price level over a period of time)
A: incorrect, that is the meaning of cost-push inflation
C: incorrect, that is the meaning of menu costs
D: incorrect, that is the meaning of demand-pull inflation

parts.text: Which one of the following best describes **consumer price index (CPI)**?

A measure of the change in the average price of a weighted basket of goods and services bought by households

rows.answer:
Correct option: **D** (A measure of the change in the average price of a weighted basket of goods and services bought by households)
A: incorrect, that is the meaning of deflation
B: incorrect, that is the meaning of cost-push inflation
C: incorrect, that is the meaning of menu costs

Prices in Ostrelia have been falling for 15 months. Shoppers are delaying purchases of cars and furniture because they expect prices to fall further.

Prices fell by 1.1% over the past year. Retail sales of cars and furniture fell by 8%. Wages are rising slowly, at about 2% a year.

Some prices have fallen because of cheaper technology and lower world oil prices. Firms with large debts say falling prices make repayments harder. The central bank's interest rate is already 0.5%.

parts.text: Which one of the following best describes **balance of payments**?
choices: When the value of money flowing out on the current account is greater than the money flowing in, e.g. imports exceed exports
The part of the balance of payments that records trade in goods and services plus primary and secondary income flows
A record of all financial transactions between one country and the rest of the world
When the value of money flowing in on the current account is greater than the money flowing out

rows.answer:
Correct option: **C** (A record of all financial transactions between one country and the rest of the world)
A: incorrect, that is the meaning of current account deficit
B: incorrect, that is the meaning of current account
D: incorrect, that is the meaning of current account surplus

Goods and services sold to other countries

A: incorrect, that is the meaning of current account deficit

The government has saved part of the export earnings in a national fund worth I\$156bn. However, the price of gas has changed by up to 30% in a single year in the past.

The top rate of income tax is 37% on incomes above H€99,000. Raising it to 45% would raise an estimated H€3bn a year. Benefits for low-income families are H€61 a week per child.

Some high earners say they may move abroad or reduce their working hours. Charities say the cost of rent and food has risen faster than benefits. The government could also spend more on free school meals and training.

parts.text: Which one of the following best describes **sustainability**?
choices: A resource that can be replaced naturally such as wind, solar energy or managed forests
Meeting the needs of the present without reducing the ability of future generations to meet their needs
A resource that will run out because it cannot be replaced, such as oil or coal
The release of harmful substances or noise into the environment which damages health and ecosystems

rows.answer:
Correct option: **B** (Meeting the needs of the present without reducing the ability of future generations to meet their needs)
A: incorrect, that is the meaning of renewable resource
C: incorrect, that is the meaning of non-renewable resource
D: incorrect, that is the meaning of pollution

parts.text: Which one of the following best describes **pollution**?
choices: A resource that will run out because it cannot be replaced, such as oil or coal
Permits giving firms the right to emit a set amount of pollution which can be bought and sold
A resource that can be replaced naturally such as wind, solar energy or managed forests
The release of harmful substances or noise into the environment which damages health and ecosystems

rows.answer:
Correct option: **D** (The release of harmful substances or noise into the environment which damages health and ecosystems)
A: incorrect, that is the meaning of non-renewable resource
B: incorrect, that is the meaning of tradable pollution permits
C: incorrect, that is the meaning of renewable resource

intro:
Rapid industrial growth in Halvoria has led to serious air pollution in its cities. The government is considering a carbon tax, stricter regulations on factories and subsidies for clean technology.

Air pollution levels in the capital are 5 times the World Health Organization guideline. Around 28,000 deaths a year are linked to air pollution. Factories and power stations produce about 61% of emissions.

The proposed carbon tax would be H€49 per tonne of carbon dioxide. Factory owners warn this could raise prices and cost jobs. Regulations would need inspectors, and the clean technology subsidy would cost H€2bn.

choices: When government spending is greater than government revenue in a year
The use of government spending and taxation to influence the economy
The total amount of money owed by the government built up from past borrowing
When government revenue is greater than government spending in a year

rows.answer:
Correct option: **B** (The use of government spending and taxation to influence the economy)
A: incorrect, that is the meaning of budget deficit
C: incorrect, that is the meaning of national debt
D: incorrect, that is the meaning of budget surplus

intro:
Tax revenue in Quorvia comes mainly from income tax, sales tax and business tax. The government wants to raise more revenue to pay for healthcare without discouraging work.

Income tax raises 37% of revenue, sales tax 36% and business tax 17%. The basic rate of income tax is 22% and sales tax is 16%. The health service needs an extra Q€4bn a year.

A 1 percentage point rise in income tax would raise Q€1bn; a 2 percentage point rise in sales tax would raise Q€3bn. Unions say sales tax hits the poor hardest, while business groups say higher income tax would reduce incentives to work.

figures.label: Extract A
figures.text:
The government of Rendova has introduced subsidies worth R\$126bn for firms producing batteries, solar panels and wind turbines. It expects new factories to create many green jobs, but other countries say the subsidies give unfair advantages.

The government expects the subsidies to create 30,000 jobs within five years. 8 new battery and solar panel factories are planned. The subsidies equal about 3% of GDP.

Other countries have complained to international trade bodies and threatened retaliation. Some economists say the money could have been spent on healthcare or used to reduce the deficit.
figures.provenance: Original fictional extract written for this question bank.

figures.label: Extract B
figures.text:
Tax revenue in Rendova comes mainly from income tax, sales tax and business tax. The government wants to raise more revenue to pay for healthcare without discouraging work.

Income tax raises 38% of revenue, sales tax 38% and business tax 16%. The basic rate of income tax is 20% and sales tax is 15%. The health service needs an extra R\$6bn a year.

A 1 percentage point rise in income tax would raise R\$1bn; a 2 percentage point rise in sales tax would raise R\$4bn. Unions say sales tax hits the poor hardest, while business groups say higher income tax would reduce incentives to work.

parts.text: Which one of the following best describes **monetary policy**?
choices: The bank that controls a country's monetary policy and issues its currency
The use of interest rates and the money supply by the central bank to influence the economy
The rate of inflation the central bank aims to achieve such as 2% a year
When the central bank creates new money to buy financial assets and increase the money supply

rows.answer:
Correct option: **B** (The use of interest rates and the money supply by the central bank to influence the economy)
A: incorrect, that is the meaning of central bank
C: incorrect, that is the meaning of inflation target
D: incorrect, that is the meaning of quantitative easing

intro:
Istrova has low productivity and 6.5% unemployment, with many vacancies unfilled because of skills shortages. The government plans to spend I\$6bn on education and training and I\$18bn on roads and railways.

There are 277,000 job vacancies, many for engineers, nurses and electricians. Output per worker in Istrova is 26% below the regional average. Around 55% of roads need repair.

The education and training spending would take about 6 years to show its full effect. The government will fund the spending by borrowing, adding to a national debt of 78% of GDP.

Business tax is currently 28%, compared with 17% in neighbouring countries. Foreign direct investment into Zentara fell by 19% last year. Firms say it takes 4 months to dismiss a worker.

Cutting the tax rate by 5 percentage points would reduce revenue by an estimated Z£2bn a year. Trade unions warn that fewer regulations could reduce job security and working conditions.

subject: economics

intro:
The government of Kaleda wants to increase economic growth by expanding its mining industry. Environmental groups warn this will increase pollution and damage forests.

The mining industry contributes 20% of GDP and employs 499,000 people. The planned expansion would add an estimated 1% to GDP growth each year.

Forests cover 54% of Kaleda, down from 64% thirty years ago. Tourism linked to forests and wildlife employs 225,000 people. Rivers near existing sites have high levels of pollution.

Accurate knowledge applied consistently, making effective use of the context and data. Chains of reasoning are well developed and balanced.
